title: Computable sufficient conditions for comparing stochastic reaction networks with mass-action or monotone kinetics
summary: Stochastic reaction networks are mathematical models with a wide range of applications in biochemistry, ecology, and epidemiology, and are often complex to analyze. Except for some special cases, it is generally difficult to predict how the abundances of all considered species evolve over time. A possible approach to address this issue is to develop tools to compare the model under study with a similar one whose behavior is better understood.
